tobacco___mosaic_virus.characteristics: Mottled light and dark green or yellow patches on leaves, sometimes with curling or stunted growth.

tomato___bacterial_leaf_spot.precautions: Use clean seed or plants, avoid working in the field when foliage is wet, disinfect tools, remove infected material, and rotate crops. Avoid overhead irrigation.
tomato___bacterial_leaf_spot.cure: There is no reliable cure once plants are infected. Copper-based sprays registered for the crop may slow spread; follow the label and local advice.
tomato___bacterial_leaf_spot.organic_remedy: Remove and destroy infected parts. Copper-based products may slow spread where registered for the crop.
tomato___bacterial_leaf_spot.characteristics: Small, dark, water-soaked spots on leaves, which can turn brown and drop out; fruit may show raised scabby spots.

tomato___early_blight.precautions: Remove and destroy infected leaves and plant debris. Space plants for airflow, avoid overhead watering late in the day, and rotate crops where practical.
tomato___early_blight.cure: Apply a fungicide that is registered for this crop in your region, following the product label and local regulations. Ask a local extension officer which product suits your situation.
tomato___early_blight.organic_remedy: Remove infected parts early. Copper- or sulfur-based products or a biofungicide may help where registered for the crop; follow the label.
tomato___early_blight.characteristics: Dark spots with concentric rings ('target spot') on older leaves first, which can yellow and drop.

tomato___late_blight.precautions: Avoid long leaf wetness: water at the base in the morning, improve drainage and airflow, and remove infected plants or debris. Cool, humid weather speeds the disease, so watch closely in such spells.
tomato___late_blight.cure: Use a fungicide registered for this disease and crop in your region, following the label and rotating products as advised. Act early, because it spreads fast in humid weather.
tomato___late_blight.organic_remedy: Remove infected leaves promptly. Copper-based products may reduce spread where registered for the crop; follow the label.
tomato___late_blight.characteristics: Large, water-soaked, dark patches on leaves and stems, often with white fuzz underneath in humid weather. It can destroy a crop quickly.

tomato___spider_mites.characteristics: Tiny yellow or white speckling on leaves, fine webbing underneath, and leaves that bronze and dry out. It is caused by pests, not a pathogen, and worsens in hot, dry weather.
tomato___spider_mites.precautions: Check the underside of leaves regularly, avoid dusty or water-stressed plants, and protect natural predators of mites.
tomato___spider_mites.cure: Use a miticide registered for this crop in your region, following the label. Ask a local extension officer which product suits your situation.
tomato___spider_mites.organic_remedy: Spray plants with a strong stream of water, and use insecticidal soap or horticultural oil where registered, following the label.

tomato___target_spot.characteristics: Brown spots with concentric rings and yellow edges on leaves, and sometimes on fruit.
